state.case_summary:
A patient in their late 40s was admitted to the hospital to receive a uterine myomectomy procedure. The patient had no history of structural heart disease, hypertension, myocarditis, or sleep apnea syndrome, and denied a family history of cardiovascular disease and sudden death. The patient had not received any pharmacologic agents that would affect cardiac rhythm.

Initial examination revealed no significant abnormalities.

- Laboratory tests: Normal levels of whole blood cells count, electrolytes, myocardial enzymes, and brain natriuretic peptide.- ECG and Imaging:  * Initial 12-lead ECG showed no abnormalities  * Chest radiographic imaging showed no abnormalities  * Echocardiographic findings showed no abnormalities  * Holter monitor recording:    Image Title: Patient Electrocardiogram Recorded by Holter Monitor During Syncope    Image Description: Recording showed a 23.8-second ventricular asystole during syncope. The rhythm strip demonstrated gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block. Asystole derived from gradually extended PR and PP intervals and was transiently suspended by a spontaneous junctional escape beat.- Electrophysiologic studies: Showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Paroxysmal complete atrioventricular block
B. Vagus-mediated paroxysmal atrioventricular block (VP-AVB)
C. Neurally mediated (vasovagal) syncope
D. Carotid sinus hypersensitivity
